  "title": "netdata image in use is spyware",
  "body": "https://github.com/titpetric/netdata/blob/master/releases/latest/scripts/build.sh#L31\r\n\r\nThe netdata image that's being used in CapRover doesn't pass the needed `--disable-telemetry` flag into the installer script when building the image, so the image contains the netdata on-by-default spyware, as documented here:\r\n\r\nhttps://docs.netdata.cloud/docs/anonymous-statistics/\r\n\r\nThese statistics are not and can not be anonymous, as they include an IP address, which is a unique identifier.  It transmits this information to Google for storage.\r\n\r\nPlease do not embed spyware in CapRover.",
  "author": "Participant 1",
  "created_at": "2019-11-25T15:38:12Z",
  "updated_at": "2024-03-28T21:55:54Z",
  "state": "closed",
  "closed_at": null,
  "issue_fetched_at": "2026-11-05T07:20:34.986313+00:00",

    "2026-11-05T07:20:34.986313+00:00"
  ],
  "expected_comment_count": 12,
  "retrieved_comment_count": 12,
  "comments_complete": true,
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": 558211345,
      "url": "https://github.com/caprover/caprover/issues/553#issuecomment-558211345",
      "created_at": "2019-11-25T15:40:11Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "I submitted a PR to that image:\r\n\r\nhttps://github.com/titpetric/netdata/pull/91"
    },
    {
      "id": 558215812,
      "url": "https://github.com/caprover/caprover/issues/553#issuecomment-558215812",
      "created_at": "2019-11-25T15:49:45Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "Please use words carefully. You're accusing NetData of being a spyware. Analytics, as long as they're anonymous, are an integral part of any software. According to PII definitions, IP alone doesn't count as PII. "
    },
    {
      "id": 558217262,
      "url": "https://github.com/caprover/caprover/issues/553#issuecomment-558217262",
      "created_at": "2019-11-25T15:53:02Z",
      "updated_at": "2019-11-25T15:54:05Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "> Analytics, as long as they're anonymous, are an integral part of any software.\r\n\r\nThis is an objectively false statement.\r\n\r\nMuch software, netdata included, works fine without analytics.  It is absolutely not *integral*.\r\n\r\n> According to PII definitions, IP alone doesn't count as PII.\r\n\r\nThis is another objectively false statement.\r\n\r\nhttps://www.irishtimes.com/business/technology/european-court-of-justice-rules-ip-addresses-are-personal-data-1.2835704\r\n\r\nAny tool that phones home to transmit telemetry *without notifying the user* or *allowing them an opportunity to opt out* is, by definition, spyware - it spies on the user for the benefit of the developer, at the expense of the user's privacy, without their consent, or, in many cases, knowledge.  There is no other criterion for defining what is or isn't spyware: that's the whole thing."
    },
    {
      "id": 558221010,
      "url": "https://github.com/caprover/caprover/issues/553#issuecomment-558221010",
      "created_at": "2019-11-25T16:01:06Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "1) By simply using CapRover, you're pulling data from dockerhub, they do have your IP.\r\n\r\n2) spyware is a strong accusation for IP collection.\r\n\r\n3) netdata isn't an integral part of CapRover. Posting this here is completely misleading. \r\n\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 558222683,
      "url": "https://github.com/caprover/caprover/issues/553#issuecomment-558222683",
      "created_at": "2019-11-25T16:04:52Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "Connecting to DockerHub is essential to functionality (i.e. downloading the `nginx` container), and does not transmit system information *beyond* IP address to them - it doesn't even tell them the accessing client is CapRover.  It's not an information leak.\r\n\r\nI encourage you to go and read the link; NetData is collecting a lot more than just IPs.  Google is receiving all of that additional data, *plus* the IP address.  At no point are NetData users (or CapRover users) notified of this, or given an opportunity to opt out or prevent this data from being transmitted (perhaps against their will, as it was in my case).  That's clearly spyware."
    },
    {
      "id": 558222916,
      "url": "https://github.com/caprover/caprover/issues/553#issuecomment-558222916",
      "created_at": "2019-11-25T16:05:23Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "I'm not sure what your objection to patching out NetData's spyware (when embedded into CapRover) is."
    },
    {
      "id": 558226247,
      "url": "https://github.com/caprover/caprover/issues/553#issuecomment-558226247",
      "created_at": "2019-11-25T16:13:15Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "I don't have an objection with regards to patching the 3rd party container. \r\n\r\nWhat I opposed with, was speeding the \"fear of being watched\" and using the term \"spyware\". Regardless, like you tweeted yourself, if you look at software world these days. Any software is a spyware as it transmit your IP, user agent and etc (excluding cookies as they can actually contain personal data). Spreading fear like this will benefit no one IMO. But we need people like you to advocate for privacy anyways, so keep up the good work. "
    },
    {
      "id": 558226695,
      "url": "https://github.com/caprover/caprover/issues/553#issuecomment-558226695",
      "created_at": "2019-11-25T16:14:19Z",
      "updated_at": "2019-11-25T16:21:09Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "> Any software is a spyware as it transmit your IP, user agent and etc (excluding cookies as they can actually contain personal data).\r\n\r\nThis is false, and a bad faith argument at that.  Web browsers are network client software.  They cannot function as a network client if they do not send and receive packets; this actually *would* be a good example of such disclosure being integral to the functionality.  It literally cannot work without it.  It's not done at the benefit of the developer and the expense of the privacy of the user.\r\n\r\nNetData (and the others I mentioned) work *perfectly fine* with their spyware portions patched out.  Their functionality isn't compromised *at all*.  I know, because I'm running these things firewalled, hosts-blocked, and reconfigured in such a way as to foil their spying.  It's quite telling that developers pretend to care about user privacy and consent, yet make us jump through ridiculous hoops to disable the spying (that benefits them and not us).  NetData doesn't even offer the option unless you install in a nonstandard fashion.\r\n\r\nThe vast majority of the software on my system does not phone home or spy on me.  Don't use \"everyone else was doing it\" as an excuse; *not* everyone else is doing it. The unethical ones are.\r\n\r\n[ An aside: think of the amount of time I have had to spend to protect my personal data - DNS blocking, firewall rules, Little Snitch dialogs, uBlock Origin.... it's dozens of hours that I could have spent working on things that are actually productive, *if vendors would just respect their limited rights to other people's computers*. ]"
    },
    {
      "id": 558228821,
      "url": "https://github.com/caprover/caprover/issues/553#issuecomment-558228821",
      "created_at": "2019-11-25T16:19:02Z",
      "updated_at": "2019-11-25T16:19:28Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "It sounds like you didn't realize that you had embedded spyware; it's a bad situation for a developer who has built a tool that helps people host things for themselves - you go to all that trouble and inconvenience and end up leaking your data to Google after all despite your work!\r\n\r\nLet's just get it fixed in CapRover so that doesn't happen anymore.  Take ownership of the failure."
    },
    {
      "id": 558230388,
      "url": "https://github.com/caprover/caprover/issues/553#issuecomment-558230388",
      "created_at": "2019-11-25T16:22:37Z",
      "updated_at": "2019-11-25T16:23:03Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "Please reopen this issue; Regardless of what your opinions on spyware are, CapRover *as it is shipping right now* phones user configuration data back to Google as soon as NetData is enabled, without notifying the user that it is doing so."
    },
    {
      "id": 558238191,
      "url": "https://github.com/caprover/caprover/issues/553#issuecomment-558238191",
      "created_at": "2019-11-25T16:40:46Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-02-16T20:22:46Z",
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "Without a simple usage analytics, NetData folks would not have been able to secure funding so that they can build such a great product for us to use for free. So if anything is unethical, it is to quote their product as a spyware. Anyways, this conversation isn't going anywhere.\r\nI added a bit to the NetData page to address your concern: https://github.com/caprover/caprover-frontend/commit/d577e941e25e64c2ca3a00fc63b24c1b2b527185\r\n\r\nMore aggressively, I'll add notes to the docs to address your privacy concerns. NetData isn't the only app that possibly sends your IP. There is, certbot, a million one-click apps, there is Docker itself and etc.\r\n\r\n------\r\n\r\n**UPDATE:**\r\nIt actually turned out that NetData analytics started from v1.12, [NetData's Readme](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/blob/a4915d80fbc1e2789a2e06a1021f1ec70f76713d/README.md) :\r\n> Starting with v1.12, Netdata collects anonymous usage information by default and sends it to Google Analytics. Read about the information collected, and learn how to-opt, on our anonymous statistics page.\r\n\r\n\r\nwhereas CapRover's built-in NetData is v1.8.\r\nhttps://github.com/caprover/caprover/blob/b1e3d49b4b2573f95f97af3498604f0994f300a6/src/utils/CaptainConstants.ts#L34\r\n\r\nHence this issue is fundamentally invalid. "
    },
    {
      "id": 558376113,
      "url": "https://github.com/caprover/caprover/issues/553#issuecomment-558376113",
      "created_at": "2019-11-25T22:49:59Z",
      "updated_at": "2019-11-26T15:49:09Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "> Without a simple usage analytics, NetData folks would have been able to secure funding so that they can build such a great product for us to use for free.\r\n\r\nThis is irrelevant, and likely untrue.  Many projects have been able to become profitable and indeed, raise money, whilst acting ethically.\r\n\r\nCertbot requires talking to an API to function and perform the task that certbot does. NetData works absolutely fine with 100% functionality without its telemetry functioning. They are nothing alike. \r\n\r\nFrom https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spyware :\r\n\r\n> Spyware is a software that aims to gather information about a person or organization, sometimes without their knowledge, and send such information to another entity without the consumer's consent. \r\n\r\nNetData did precisely that, without my knowledge and without my consent. It fits the textbook definition of spyware. It’s fact, not hyperbole. \r\n"
    }
  ],
